draft_evidence.quote:
He put Lira into Oryn's hands and let the box go off his back.

Shadow-adjacent. Once.

He had not used it on this side of the Line; he had held it through a country with a ledger and a ferry west, and there was no public here — four people who knew where it came from, a healer who had found nothing in him three times, and eight animals. He thinned. It was Seln's — the presence going out of him like a lamp turned down, the movement folded into the dark — and he crossed ten strides of grass through the middle of a pack turning to a woman's voice, and not one head turned to him. If it counted as a declaration, nothing on the floor came to it. He did not have a sentence for that either. He put it on the shelf.

He got the hound by the loose skin at the back of its neck and a hind leg and heaved.

The Iron read gave him the ground under his boots and he used all of it. The animal came off her chest with its jaws still working and its teeth coming off her throat, and he turned with it and threw it as far as a man throws a thing that weighs what he does, into the south scrub, and it landed and rolled and was up. Karis lay on her back with her mouth open, and no sound came out of it now.

Seven heads in the scrub, and the one he had thrown, were turned to where the sound had been.

He knew what they followed. He had learned it on a river from the thing that did not happen: the loudest declaration, and absent one, the loudest sound, and absent that, whichever thing on the floor committed first. They had never met a thing on this floor that could declare. He had been the only thing on it that could since the stone, and had told nobody, and the sentence he owed them was sixty meters west and he was going to have to run it before he wrote it.

He stopped holding.

---

Wind-adjacent, full.

The burst went through him as it had gone through Lira on the rim, the whole of it, the legs and the back and the breath — and did not land as nothing. It landed as twelve paces of grass in the time a breath takes, the scrub going flat and white either side of him with the wind of it, the loudest thing that had ever been inside this circle, on purpose, west, past the pack, along the lane toward a stone in a rut.

Every head turned.

Eight animals that had never in their lives sensed a declaration on this ground turned to it, all at once, as seven had turned on a river to a bead of white on a girl's fingers. Then he was in the landing lock — the fixed one-count, the beat he could not price a hit inside — and he heard the scrub come after him.

Wind was a burst and a lock and then a body running, and a body running was nearly nothing to them. So he did what he had not done since a matting floor against a Gold-tier woman: he spent everything, one after another, so that there was never a breath in which he was not the loudest thing on the floor.

Pressure-adjacent, because it was loud and he needed it for nothing else. Ember-adjacent, one point of ignition held out at arm's length as he ran, Karis's, a bead of white that lit the lane five paces round and made the scrub either side go still and then come on harder. Blade-adjacent, Ephram's, which had nothing to cut and rang anyway. Storm-adjacent, Daeva's, the pressure-differential seeded ahead of him along the lane so that the air went wrong for ten paces and every fragment in him that was not Storm rang with it as a struck pan rings. Anchor-adjacent, let off its hold, looking west. He ran through the middle of his own noise with the Iron read under his soles giving him every root and stone in the dark, and the calf hot, and the ribs stopping his breath at the tape on every stride, and behind him eight grey shapes came after the only declaration they had ever met on their floor.

One reached him in the second lock.

A second burst at forty, and the hound came out of the south scrub inside it, low, at the leg, and he took it on the shoulder instead — Compression-adjacent, Reydan's, at contact, the force of the animal going into him and through him and out along his own frame into the ground — and it went over him and was up, and he was up, and it turned with the rest and came on.

Twenty meters.

The stone in the rut ahead of him, two fists of it, dark against the grey; Seln a stride beyond it on the road, standing; Brom beyond Seln with Karis over his shoulder and the bow in his cut hand; Oryn and Lira on the road's far edge, Lira on her back, Oryn on her knees; the mule, hipshot, exactly where it had been left.

comparison_evidence.quote: The lane, then, in the order Seln had put them: Seln somewhere ahead in the scrub; Karis; Oryn; Lira on Cael's shoulder with the ankle going down wrong every second stride; Brom at the rear with the bow wound and his right hand held oddly on the stock. Cael had the middle box on his own back by then, because Brom needed both hands and Karis needed the box.

findings.consequence: At sixty meters, Cael leaves Karis on the ground, immediately bursts west past the pack, and takes a second Wind burst at forty. Brom begins behind the formation and must first reach Karis, lift her with a cut hand, then carry her sixty meters; Oryn must move Lira the same distance on a bitten arm and failed ankle. Both are already beyond the line before the Wind-assisted Cael reaches twenty meters. The climactic retreat therefore contains an impossible speed/elapsed-time jump at the exact point the reader needs positions and cause to be clearest.
findings.repair_target: Make the supporting group's sixty-meter movement and Cael's pursuit route/timing causally legible while preserving the packet's required state that the whole unit is already over when he crosses, Karis is carried by Brom, Lira is moved by the group, and Cael leads the pack out.

findings.repair_target: Preserve every word and order of the packet's verbatim closing exchange while bringing the one-word-paragraph count to two or fewer through attribution or paragraphing that remains clear in audio.

concerns: Taste only / packet tension: the packet's opening_state says the party is approximately 140 meters inside, while Chapter 10's measured geometry places the ring's west lip roughly 187 meters inside and the must-include choreography requires Brom and Lira to fight on that lip. The draft sensibly privileges the measured lip and uses 140 meters as a retreat waypoint. Because the work order itself pulls in both directions and '~140' is not repeated in must_include, this is not raised as a defect; a human may wish to normalize the card later.

Taste only: the post-fight Power Log is useful continuity infrastructure, but it repeats the win mechanism, full fragment inventory, all six injury states, witness count, and priority after the prose has already rendered each clearly. At the upper end of the length band, a later compression pass could test how much of that recapitulation the chapter needs without weakening the required honest inventory.

Taste only: 'the loudest thing' and the explanation of declaration/sound priority recur several times across the run. The repetition is functional tactical tracking, not a capped tic, but the audio pass should preserve escalation so the mechanism does not feel re-explained after the reader already understands it.
strengths: Yes: the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. Quiet ground is not explained in a lore block; it constrains declarations, a healer's hands, pack ecology, the unit's volume, the value of a crossbow, the exact position of a lattice, and the seasonal price of a mend. The world's rule is learned by what bodies and tools can or cannot do.

Yes: the set piece is memorable, and terrain is load-bearing well beyond the minimum. The hand-high fused lip removes a hound's drive and turns Lira's ankle; the cord-line supplies the uncut lane; scrub makes sound visible without making hounds visible; the distant stone is an objective; the sharp boundary restores five Paths; and the one meter inside it becomes Karis's ignition wall. The clean win sentence is: Cael removed the pack's ability to fight where its prey could not declare by becoming the one declaration it could follow out.

The core tactical inversion is excellent and fully earned. Chapter 3 taught declaration bait, loudest-target behavior, the cut dog, and pack commitment; Chapter 11 turns each fact over under a new constraint. 'The ford turned over: the declaration ran, and the killing was a line' is a precise receipt, not an after-the-fact excuse.

Brom's lip exchange is especially strong. The prose establishes balance before force—forefeet landing below expected hind-foot level—then lets a Pathless fighter win one beat with planted weight, good footwork, and a haft. It characterizes competence without smuggling Iron Skin back into the Quiet.

Oryn's failure and recovery land through procedure. The stopped count, blood to the wrist, cloth and knees, exact two-sentence order, resumed count at the stride, one-hour mend, vascular/deep-tear findings, and load prohibition make the cost legible in both medical and emotional registers.

Character tactics remain sharply differentiated under a shared survival problem: Seln calls geometry in flat fragments, Brom holds and bolts, Lira runs the style stripped to bone, Karis builds the wall voiceless, Oryn reaches the hurt, and Cael turns a catalogue of prior mechanisms into one decision.

The secret becomes relationship pressure without premature disclosure. All five witnesses are named by position, nobody theorizes, Lira's arm correctly outranks the revelation, and the final 'Later' exchange changes trust while deferring explanation to its assigned chapter.

The injury and fragment accounting are unusually disciplined. All nine fragments have established sources and uses; the anomaly is not promoted; Shadow's seal is honored; the full-suite bill is paid; every wound is side-specific and carried; two dead and seven open are recorded rather than rounded into victory.

Production is otherwise clean: 5,194 words is within tolerance; metadata, summary-substitution, modern-register, feeling/growth, pitch-prohibition, and named tic greps return zero for Chapter 11; Book 7 remains under every book-level phrase cap; names pass the registry ear check; attribution survives audio; and the dialogue ending differs structurally from Chapter 10's log ending.
